title: God Has Ascended amid Shouts of Joy
superscription: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.

verses.text: Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph.
How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!
He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah
God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn.
Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!
For God is King of all the earth; sing profound praises to Him.
God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne.
The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.

context.author: The title names the sons of Korah, a family of Levites descended from the Korah who rebelled against Moses (Numbers 16). His sons did not die with him (Numbers 26:11), and their descendants became gatekeepers and singers at the Temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph. How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!” (vv.1-2). He chose Israel’s inheritance (v.4). Then a procession: “God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn” (v.5). “Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!” (v.6). “God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne” (v.8). At the end the nobles of the nations gather “as the people of the God of Abraham” (v.9).
context.custom: Coronations were celebrated with clapping, shouting and the ram’s horn (2 Kings 11:12; 1 Kings 1:39). The ark, God’s throne, was carried up to Zion with shouting and the shofar (2 Samuel 6:15), which may be the picture behind “God has ascended.” Kings of conquered nations came to pay homage to the great king.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 48 praises Zion, “the city of the great King.”
context.timelineBible: Christians have long read v.5 on Ascension Day, when Jesus was taken up into heaven (Acts 1:9). God promised Abraham that “all the families of the earth will be blessed through you” (Genesis 12:3), the hope of v.9. Revelation celebrates when “the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ” (Revelation 11:15).

gospelParallels.note: He was taken up before their eyes.
The kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ.

otBackground.note: The ark brought up with shouts and the horn.
All the families of the earth will be blessed.

overview.summary: All peoples are called to clap and shout as God goes up to His throne with the sound of the horn, King over all the earth and the nations.
overview.settingLine: A coronation procession with the ram’s horn.

archaeology.t: Ram’s horns are pictured on later Jewish art; the instrument is still blown.
Assyrian palace reliefs show vassal kings paying homage.

overview.discussion: The psalm calls “all you peoples” to praise (v.1). How does God’s reign over all nations shape the way I see people from other nations?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: The sons of Korah
